At seven in the evening. Officiating rabbi: JAKOB JOEL SPIRO, rabbi of Klimontow.
Banns read at the Klimontow synagogue on 2, 9 and 16 August 1834.
Witnesses: Lewek Nachmanowicz Kanar, 46, and Jokel Bursztyn, 52 - both szkolnicy
(synagogue beadles) of Klimontow. Both parents present gave oral consent.

Not found in the Klimontow marriage index (covered 1826-77). Likely registered in the
bride's town, which is unidentified.

Seven children documented from birth acts read in the original: Malka Blima 1845,
Chaja Laja 1847, Chaim 1854, Fajga Perla 1856, Dawid Jakob 1858, Dawid Herszl 1861,
Szymcha 1863, Haskiel 1865, Necha 1867. Of these the register also records the deaths
of Fajga Perla (28/1857, aged one), Dawid Hersz (30/1862, aged one and a half),
Szymcha (11/1864, aged one), Chaskiel (52/1865, aged six months) and Necha (19/1869).
The household was destroyed in 1867: both parents died that year, and the baby Necha
followed in 1869.

Marriage act 24/1884. ** The single highest-value document still to be obtained: a
marriage act names the parents of both spouses, i.e. two further generations at once. **
13 Aug 2026: the JRI index row for this act was re-pulled with the parent columns
switched on (legacy.jri-poland.org, hidecols=0) and ** it is empty of parents. ** In
the Opatow batch the parent columns exist for 1846-1884 acts but are blank from about
1885 on, and 1884 already falls in the blank zone. So no index shortcut exists here:
only a copy of the act itself will name Gella's parents, and with them the bridge (if
any) between this family and the documented GINSBERG-LUBLINER cluster of Opatow, which
is deliberately NOT entered in this file. See findings/049.

(probable) The two Tobiasz births are assigned to this couple on the strength of the
sequence - marriage 1884, births 1885, 1889, all Wajsblum, all Opatow - not on a
stated parentage. The acts are unread because Opatow is unscanned online at the free
tier (GenBaza holds the register; scans blocked pending an account, findings/050).
** 14 Aug 2026: Bajla-Szajndla (@I24@), formerly the third child here on the same
sequence argument, is REMOVED - two independent Pages of Testimony name her father
Rafael, not Moszek (findings/053-058; see @F60@). With her goes the premise that
birth act 8/1892 belongs to this family. Reading that act is now the direct test:
its parent names will either confirm Rafael and Fajga or reopen this question. **
Alter (@I67@) is ADDED on the opposite grade: for him the parentage IS stated -
he declared himself "Son" of this couple in the 1966 necrology entries he supplied.
** 14 Aug 2026, later: the second Tobiasz (@I23@) also moves to the stated-parentage
grade - his 1909 Stopnica marriage row (act 25/1909, @S83@) names Moszek and Gela as
his parents. Only @I22@ now rests on the sequence argument alone. **

NOT FOUND. Absent from the Opatow marriage index (covered 1899-1917) and from the
Klimontow marriage index. The one promising row - Klimontow 3/1912, bride Szajndla
Wajcblum - turned out to have Lejbus Penczyna as groom, not a Rywenbajrych. So either
they married in a third town, or after 1917, beyond the indexed range.

(documented) Married by 1947 - the Kreis Schwabmuenchen list of that year has them
consecutively as a couple, and the 1948 emigration manifest records Alter as
married, aged 44. ** No marriage record has been found: not the date, not the
place. It falls somewhere between the liberation and 1947, most likely in Poland
or in the Bavarian displaced-persons world. **

No children are known. None appear beside them on the 1947 list, none on the
Canadian voters lists, and neither gravestone names a child. That is an absence of
evidence in thin sources, not evidence of absence - the Toronto obituaries and the
Apter Friendly Society section have not been searched for them.

(documented) The family stands on three legs, each independent of the others:
(1) the 1921 Opatow town register, read in findings/022, which put Bejla under
Rafael and Fajga; (2) Moshe's five Pages of one day in 1957 - he calls Bejla and
Reizel "Brother" and their husbands "Brother-in-law", making him their sibling and
the parents his own; (3) Shlomo's independent 1955 Pages naming Szoszana's parents
Rafael and Tzipora. Discovered in this order: 022 first raised Rafael; 053-054
read Moshe's forms; 056-058 exhausted Yad Vashem, merged Reizel with Szoszana and
closed the sibling list. NO OTHER CHILDREN are attested anywhere searched; the
list is closed to current knowledge, not proven complete. Marriage: nothing found;
Opatow marriage scans for the plausible years sit in the GenBaza gap (1845-1877)
or behind its account wall.

** THE OUTSTANDING TEST: Opatow birth act 8/1892, first item in the Sandomierz
letter. If its parents read Rafael and Fajga, this family gains its first
contemporaneous civil record; if not, Bejla's birth act is unfound and the year
1891/92 rests on the memorial list and the Pages alone. **

Inferred from the elder child's birth. Both spouses' Pages agree the family counted
two children ("2" written independently by both informants). All four were murdered
at Treblinka in 1942; the whole branch ended there.

Piatek marriage act 6/1864 (JRI index). The act itself has NOT been read; it is
the key unread act - it will name both sets of parents.
See albert/findings/032-piatek-buzowski.md.

Piatek marriage act 6/1833 (JRI index). Linkage of Abram to this couple is
PROBABLE, not documented - see the note on Berek (I75).

Marriage act 75/1894, cyrkul V. Reference 72/200/0/-/89, Archiwum Panstwowe w
Warszawie; scan 38 of 189 in szukajwarchiwach unit 12482469.

Dated 6/18 February 1894; sealed by the Justice of the Peace of the 2nd district,
Warsaw. Witnesses: Szamaj Wajnberg, about 57, of ul. Ostrowska, and Abram Renkal(?),
29, of ul. Smocza - both streets in the Jewish quarter. David signed in his own hand,
with a signature in Hebrew beside it.
They met in a camp, by family account.

Marriage act 25/1909. The groom's row reads "Tobjasz WAJSBLUM, M 20, b. Opatow,
single, parents Moszek WAJSBLUM, Gela GINSBURG" - the index itself states his
parents; see the notes at @F10@ and @I23@ for what that upgrades. Stopnica is also
the town of the Kac family cluster (findings/063); no link between that cluster and
this marriage is asserted. Whether the couple had children is unknown - Stopnica
births after 1909 have not been searched for them.

Marriage act 20/1849, Radoszyce Jewish register - the CRARG transcription names both
sets of parents, which is what carries the whole 5x-generation above this couple.
Known children (all Radoszyce-register births at Zagdansk unless noted): Kalma b. 1850
(d. 1855), ESTER GITLA b. 1851 (@I41@), Laja b. 1852, Sora b. 1852 (d. at 4 months),
Sandal/Aleksander b. ~1856 (d. 1930 Kielce), Mortka Szlama b. 1858, Aron b. 1859
(probably the Aron Cukier of Nowo-Zagnanska 7, Kielce, alive 1930), Brandla (d. 1862),
Hil b. 2 Jan 1862, Sora b. 1 Feb 1865. The mother-name shifts across these acts are
the "two Rywkas" question - see the note at @I70@. Only Ester Gitla is entered as an
individual; the siblings await the resolution of that question and Amotz's decision.

Six children of Aron and Tauba, of Ruda Strawczynska, are documented in their marriage
rows in the Radoszyce register: Abram ~1821 (@I78@), Mortka ~1823 (@I81@), Mosiek
~1824 (@I85@), KIWA ~1827 (@I69@), Chaim Wolf 1834 (@I91@) and Laja ~1839 (@I99@).
The sibling tie is stated outright in Laja's 1857 act - "living with her brother Kiwa
Cukier, Zagdansk" - and Chaim Wolf's parentage is repeated independently in the
Radoszyce residents' book (@S88@). All six were entered as individuals on 15 Aug 2026
(findings/090); before that date only Kiwa was.

Marriage act 16/1844, Radoszyce Jewish register. The act names the groom's parents as
Aron and Tauba Moskowicz - one of the two rows that document Tauba's maiden surname.

Marriage act 17/1844, Radoszyce Jewish register - the same session as his brother
Abram's act 16/1844.
Marriage act 9/1846, Radoszyce Jewish register.

Marriage act 3/1867: Jakob Hil Cukier, 19, of Ruda, son of Mosiek Cukier and Ryfka
nee Norenberg [Grynberg], and Ruchla Feldsztejn, 16, of Ruda Strawczynska.

Marriage act 18/1858: Hajm Wolf Cukier, 19, of Ruda Strawczynska, "son of Aron
[deceased] and Tauba", and Kajla Zlotowicz.

The household stayed at Radoszyce and lost four children young - two of them to the
cholera of August 1873, thirteen days apart.
